chunks: From him, from Aḥmad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Qāsim ibn al-Walīd, who said:

I asked him about a man for whom it became clear, while he was in the salat (prayer), that he was facing other than the qiblah. He said: He should turn to face it when that is established. But if he has already finished it, then he does not repeat it.

key_terms.إِذَا ثَبَتَ: when it becomes established or confirmed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer) being performed at the time of discovering the mistake
key_terms.غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ: other than the proper direction of the qiblah
key_terms.فَرَغَ: he completed or finished the prayer
key_terms.فَلَا يُعِيدُهَا: he does not repeat that prayer
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُهَا: he turns to face the qiblah

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he realizes during salat (prayer) that he was facing other than the qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who discovers during salat (prayer) that he is facing other than the qiblah. If the error becomes clear while the prayer is ongoing, he turns toward the qiblah; if he has already completed the prayer, he does not repeat it.
